output_json.diff_review: Reviewed patch_only.diff in full. All 8 changed files are directly relevant to the CWE-094 fix: MappingUtil.java (new loadClass helper + refactored instanceFlippingStrategy), PropertyFactory.java (createProperty now calls MappingUtil.loadClass(pType, Property.class) before getConstructor/newInstance), XmlParser.java, PropertiesParser.java, YamlParser.java (flip-strategy sinks now call MappingUtil.loadClass(...,FlippingStrategy.class).newInstance(); property-type sinks delegate to PropertyFactory.createProperty instead of duplicating unguarded Class.forName+getConstructor logic), ConsoleOperations.java (both HTTP-driven strategy sinks in createFeature and updateFlippingStrategy now use MappingUtil.loadClass), and two test files adding regression coverage (MappingUtilsTest, PropertyFactoryTest) that assert the attacker class's constructor never fires before the base-type check rejects it. No unrelated files touched, no broad/unrelated behavior changes, no weakening of the POV or vulnerable functionality removed without justification — the fix is a minimal, uniformly-applied base-type check inserted before every reflective construction call site named in the alert's traces. The .security-pipeline/pov/ directory is untouched by the patch (only new PoV artifacts, not modified).
output_json.pov_result: Independently reproduced both states by stashing/unstashing the patch in the worktree and rerunning `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` via the docker wrapper: pre-patch (git stash) → stdout "VULNERABLE: MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy reflectively constructed attacker-controlled class ... even though it does not implement FlippingStrategy", exit code 0. Post-patch (git stash pop, restored) → stdout "NOT VULNERABLE: attacker-controlled class name was rejected before construction; no side effect was observed.", exit code 1. This matches the orchestrator's own pov_before_patch/pov_after_patch logs exactly.
output_json.regression_result: Orchestrator ran full regression suites (ff4j-core: 1125 tests, ff4j-config-properties: 86 tests, ff4j-config-yaml: 117 tests, ff4j-web: 3 tests, ff4j-utils-json: 21 tests) all exit_code 0, 0 failures/errors. I independently reran a targeted subset (MappingUtilsTest, PropertyFactoryTest, XmlParserTest under ff4j-core -am) via the docker wrapper and confirmed exit code 0 with no failures.
output_json.summary: Patch adds a single choke-point MappingUtil.loadClass(className, expectedType) that resolves a class and enforces expectedType.isAssignableFrom(rawClazz) BEFORE any newInstance()/Constructor.newInstance() call, and wires it into every reflective-construction sink named in the alert: MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy, XmlParser.parseFlipStrategy and property-type parsing, PropertiesParser flip-strategy/property-type parsing, YamlParser flip-strategy/property-type parsing, PropertyFactory.createProperty (String,String constructor sink used by JSON/Mongo paths too), and ConsoleOperations' two HTTP-driven strategy-instantiation sites. Duplicate inline Class.forName+getConstructor logic in XmlParser/PropertiesParser/YamlParser was removed in favor of delegating to the now-hardened PropertyFactory.createProperty, eliminating rather than just patching each duplicate. Two new JUnit regression tests assert (via a static side-effect flag) that a foreign class's constructor never runs before the base-type check throws.
